title: Note: your first step into immersion
summary: A walk through a short native fable, as a way to move from theory to real Japanese material.

blocks.text: This episode is not a grammar topic. It shows how to start working with real Japanese made for Japanese readers: a short, simple fable about a greedy dog, read sentence by sentence. Even a children's story contains words you have never met, so the method matters more than the story.

items: Pick material that is short, simple and not rewritten for learners.
Take one sentence at a time and find its engine and main carriage before looking up details.
Expect new vocabulary: children's stories use many words that textbooks skip.
Once the text is clear, listen to the audio again and again so the rhythm and the words settle in.

blocks.text: The episode points out that many of the structures from earlier lessons appear right away in a tiny story, such as modifiers before nouns and verbs ending in a helper. Use the video as a model for how to break down your own first reading.
